core.text: Hypothesis: concurrent contact between the rotational flow and low-to-high syringe transport contributes to the sample outcome. Define the tested interface as their temporal overlap. Retain rotation and low-to-high redistribution in both arms; ablate commanded overlap by transferring during motor-off intervals. Shared-volume history survives, so this cannot establish removal of every material interface.

Proposed paired trials use nominal 300 rpm during seconds 0-15, 30-45, 60-75 and 90-105: sixty total stirring seconds. Each arm also performs three marked 10 mL low-position withdrawals and upper-side returns, each completed within five seconds. Coupled transfers occupy seconds 10-15, 40-45 and 70-75. Ablated transfers occupy seconds 25-30, 55-60 and 85-90, after ten seconds commanded off. Camera checks are recorded independently of operation. Neither parent is omitted.

Use three fresh paired comparisons within six trials, reversing arm order across pairs, fixed addition location, one dye bottle, locked camera, the prescribed recipe and spill tray. Both arms finish at second 105 and begin depth sampling at second 120; alternate sampling order and complete withdrawals within ten seconds. Report raw attenuation, normalized spread, transfer timing, commanded duration, surface depression, speck frames and failures. Proposed success is final spread at most 4 percent; stable images do not establish it.

residue.text: Transient 900 rpm specks and fluctuating images remain unexplained. These observations neither identify bubbles nor establish an agitation-renewed feedback loop; matched 900 rpm final samples are absent.

One stipulated 300 rpm run achieved approximately 2.4 percent final-vial spread without syringe redistribution. Combined-operation success and any interface advantage remain hypotheses. Reference repeatability is not concentration calibration, and broader conditions remain untested.

Motor-off does not guarantee cessation of bulk circulation. Transfer timing and transient gradient state differ between arms; inspect moving frames and report residual motion. Similar outcomes would question necessity of commanded concurrency, not prove hydrodynamic independence. Different outcomes alone cannot separate coupling from timing or transport disturbance.

tension.account_a: Hypothesis: concurrent interaction is necessary for this fixed pair of parent doses to reach the sample target.
tension.account_b: Incompatible hypothesis: temporal overlap is dispensable; these retained parent doses suffice when staggered.
tension.prediction_a: Coupled trials would meet the 4 percent target while staggered trials would reproducibly exceed it, conditional on effective overlap ablation.
tension.prediction_b: Staggered trials would also reproducibly meet the target despite removal of commanded overlap. Failure of both would leave these accounts unresolved.
